newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Strikes may push Seoul Jan trade deficit to record. [CORRECTED 3:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Strikes may push Seoul Jan trade deficit to record. [CORRECTED 3:41 GMT]

text.p: South Korea's January trade deficit could hit a record high of $3.9 billion if strikes disrupting major export industries last until the end of the month, a trade ministry spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman said the deficit was originally forecast at $3.2 billion.
The previous record trade shortfall was $3.28 billion in August 1996. It hit $2.13 billion last January.
"Export losses from the strikes are currently at around $441 million, and we see that rising to $645 million by the end of the month," he said.
(Corrects figures for export losses from billion to million)
